Subject: Q3 renewal: mapped uplift proposal + latency & ROI snapshot

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As promised, attached is a short usage snapshot for Q2 (tokens by route, 95th percentile latency by model, and cost per 1M tokens) plus a one-page ROI sketch showing current spend vs. proposed commit tiers. High-level takeaways: 1) Atlas is seeing sustained growth in batch embedding jobs (peak windows: 10–11am PT) which drives the majority of token volume; 2) average generation latency on dev models is ~180ms; production model p95 typically sits ~360ms — we have room to improve with batching + prefix caching; 3) the current run-rate projects to ~1.9x of your present commit by renewal date.

I've sketched three options in the attachment: conservative (no term change), staged uplift (6–9 month step increases + burst credits), and committed uplift (12-month, discounted). The staged uplift preserves flexibility while capping unit price increases — we recommend the staged path for a product that is still iterating on prompt mix.

Can you share which internal stakeholders we should loop for legal/finance? If helpful, I can prepare a simple amendment that maps traffic tiers to concrete monthly commit numbers and an SLA addendum for latency during peak windows.

Attachments:
- redwood_q2_usage_snapshot.pdf (report, 3 pages)
- q3_uplift_sketch.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

Thanks,

Jordan —

Answers below (TL;DR at top):
- TL;DR: p50 -> ~120ms, p95 -> ~340ms with prefix cache enabled + staged uplift and current model mixes. Burst credits are a separate bucket that only apply when committed capacity is exceeded. We can run the 2-week canary with Redwood CS + your ops; Redwood will own routing toggles and observability during the test.

Details:
1) Latency expectations: We tested a similar workload last quarter (customer "HelioHealth") and saw p50/p95 improve by ~25–30% after enabling prefix caching and enabling continuous micro-batching tuned for your peak window. For Atlas's distribution (70% embeddings, 30% generate), our conservative estimate is p50 ~120ms, p95 ~340ms for production models at your projected Q3 volumes. We can provide a small synthetic run in our staging to validate.

2) Burst credits: They are a separate consumable bucket (e.g., 200M tokens) applied before overage billing. When consumed, usage shows in the dashboard as "burst" and does not reduce the committed baseline. If burst is exhausted, excess tokens are charged at on-demand rate. We usually recommend a 10–15% burst buffer for products with spiky batch jobs.

3) Canary plan: Redwood will provision a canary route that maps a percentage of traffic to the upgraded runtime (caching + batching enabled). We'll provide a shared dashboard with p50/p95, error-rate, and token-cost metrics. Rollback is a single routing flag flip. Redwood CS (I suggest Mina + ops) will be on-call for the two-week window; we will run daily 9am PT standups for the first 3 days then every-other-day check-ins.

Attachments:
- redwood_q2_usage_snapshot.pdf (re-sent for reference)
- pricing_commit_options_v3.xlsx (proposed tiers, 3 options)

Pricing note: For a 12-month commit at ~2.0x current run-rate we can offer a 16% unit discount vs. on-demand. Staged uplift pricing is +8% unit economics vs. the committed discount in the early stage, with step-downs as volume ramps.

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Sara / Atlas procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal testing and the numbers below, we recommend the staged uplift option with an initial 3-month bridge that includes a 200M-token burst credit. Summary: 
- Month 0–3: baseline commit = 1.0x current run-rate, burst = 200M tokens, unit price = on-demand less 6%
- Month 4–6: baseline commit increases to 1.5x, unit price steps down to on-demand less 10%
- Month 7–12: baseline commit moves to 2.0x, unit price steps to on-demand less 14%

Expected performance after enabling prefix cache + micro-batching during canary: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~340ms (within your 400ms requirement). Canary plan: Redwood will provision a canary route, share a dashboard, and run daily checks first three days. Rollback is immediate via routing flag.
